Nīḷāsūkta
------------------------------------------
This short सूक्त appears in the Taittirīya Saṁhitā (

). It is on Nīḷādevī, the third consort of विष्णु. She is identified with अदिति, the मोथेर् of all gods.
She is the personification of karuṇā (compassion and grace) of God. She is also the power that manifests through सूर्य (the Sun), चन्द्र (the मोओन्) and अग्नि (the Fire).
A brief summary of the सूक्त may now be given:
I take refuge in Nīḷādevī. O goddess! Please speak!
O God, who is the supreme creator! That goddess who is the firm refuge of the devotees, who is the consort of विष्णु, who is compassionate, who is the mistress of the universe, the repository of all types of strength and power, who is worshipped by the living beings in their minds, who grants all the objects of enjoyment, may that deity give us lordship and bless us with bliss.
May बृहस्पति (the गुरु of the gods), वायु (the god of wind), the prāṇas (life forces) in the body, and Nīḷādevī who is the supporter of the quarters and the earth, who is the mistress of the world and a consort of विष्णु, preach to us what is good for us!
Iconographical works, following the Pāñcarātra tradition, describe Nīḷā or Nīḷādevī as dark-blue in complexion, like the blue-lotus. She is clothed in blue garments and richly bedecked with ornaments. In her four hands she holds two lotuses in two, the other two exhibiting the abhaya and varada mudrās, mudrās assuring freedom from fear and giving boons.
